statement: The client's host is pinned to Node 20, so relay must not use Node 22+ features (for example --experimental-strip-types or require of ESM).
Do not add new dependencies without asking the user first.
Tests use the language's built-in runner (node:test, unittest); no jest, vitest or pytest.
The retry queue lives in Redis (ioredis).
Relay API timestamps are epoch milliseconds, because the client SDK expects ms.
The HMAC check was extracted into a shared helper in src/lib/ that new provider routes should reuse.
Keep diffs to what the task needs; do not reformat or refactor unrelated files.
No pandas or polars: the worker box has 512 MB of RAM.
Send 10,000 rows per warehouse request.
Use the exponential-backoff package for retry delays.
The exponential-backoff package was rejected as too heavy; backoff is hand-written in relay.
The admin API must never return webhook payload bodies (client contract, PII).
Retries live in a Postgres deliveries table; Redis was dropped because ops won't run it, so no Redis or other queue service.
Store timestamps as UTC ISO-8601 strings; convert to local time only in reports.
Ops already ran the prod backfill of old retries into the deliveries table; it is not a deploy step.
Admin list pagination is cursor-based, because offset pagination breaks under concurrent inserts.
Admin API: list, get and attempts endpoints are done; pagination of GET /admin/deliveries is next.
Vendor column mappings live in one registry module so new vendors are added there, not parsed ad hoc.
Multiprocessing was tried and reverted because it broke dedupe ordering.
The vendor_a 2024-2025 history is already loaded into the warehouse; do not reload it.
Send 2,000 rows per warehouse request, because the warehouse rejects requests over 4 MB.
The vendor_b file fails on encoding; the next step is a cp1252 fallback in the reader.
